project_specification.project_name: nullius — process-based node evaluation (use the host's cores)
project_specification.addition_summary: Node evaluation is GIL-bound pure Python: alignment and validation over cached closes, plus the materializer. The thread pool from 389a095 therefore gives about one core of throughput. With evaluation_workers=8 on the 16-core host, each 32-root archive campaign of 2026-10-09 took about 65 min (_run-log.md Run 10); the 8 threads mostly wait on the GIL. M3 needs many more financial worlds (architecture §10.6: the gate is judged on financial holdout worlds), so evaluation throughput bounds the whole research loop.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / SQLite / gVisor runsc sandbox / pytest.
existing_context.test_baseline: main at df3b55e: gate 1663 passed; orchestrator 548 passed 5 skipped.
existing_context.conventions: Follow CLAUDE.md. Pools today: - _campaign.py ~:303-375: root evaluation on a ThreadPoolExecutor, with results released in planting order and history_store.persist under a write_lock. - _dispatch_round ~:254-293 calls discovery.run_batch with a NodeWorker (_worker.py ~:173), which authors (LLM I/O), records the attempt, then calls evaluator.evaluate. - LiveEvaluator.evaluate (__init__.py ~:138-211) calls create_app() per call, resolves the target route, sidecar and ledger, builds a SubtreeOracle and calls evaluate_node. - EvaluationContext is a frozen dataclass of paths and values, plus SnapshotMount (no file descriptors) and _LazyCloses (__slots__). Rebuilding it per worker with load_evaluation_context() is safest. - Module caches (_CLOSE_CACHE, _PANELS) are per process. - evaluate_node's SQLite writes (ledger debit, tripwire verdicts, stability, node metrics, poison) each open their own connection. - gVisor container ids are uuid4 under one state root.

category.name: Evaluation Throughput
category.feature: System evaluates nodes in worker processes, so that a campaign's evaluation runs on as many cores as evaluation_workers names instead of one GIL. - New orchestrator._process_pool.ProcessEvaluator has the same .evaluate(node_id, campaign_id, depth, code) -> NodeEvaluation shape as LiveEvaluator. - It uses a ProcessPoolExecutor with the spawn context and max_workers = evaluation_workers. - Its initializer loads the evaluation context once per worker (load_evaluation_context with the parent's environment) and composes the app once (create_app()), so the sidecar, target route and ledger are resolved once per worker, not per node. - Each task runs the existing evaluate_node and returns the NodeEvaluation. It must pickle, so verify NodeMetrics, ScoreRecord and the pipeline's exceptions round-trip, and make any that do not picklable. - The evaluation config gains evaluation_mode: "process" (the default) or "thread". "thread" keeps today's in-process LiveEvaluator. It is documented in the example config. build_live_evaluator returns the evaluator the mode names. - The existing thread pools in _campaign.py and run_batch stay. Each thread's .evaluate() now blocks on the process pool, so authoring and LLM I/O stay on parent threads, and history_store and emit stay in the parent in their existing deterministic order. - SQLite writes inside evaluate_node stay in the worker. Every connection those stores open sets busy_timeout of at least 30 s, so concurrent writers wait rather than fail. - Memory: per-worker caches are bounded by the existing max_history_days panel. The pool's worker count is min(evaluation_workers, cpu_count - 2), and the cap is logged. - The pool shuts down cleanly at campaign end and on SIGTERM, with no orphan workers or runsc processes. - test_process_pool_evaluation.py, with a module-level picklable stub executor configured through the environment, covers: - modes "process" and "thread" produce identical persisted node rows, ledger rows (set-equal) and node_evaluated event order on an 8-root offline campaign - process mode with 4 workers runs a CPU-bound stub at least 2.5x faster than thread mode on 8 nodes - a node raising in a worker surfaces as that node's failure without cancelling its siblings - shutdown leaves no child processes It passes under pytest-xdist.
